questions.question: What is the relative base for the 'rem' unit in CSS?
options: The font-size of the root <html> element
The width of the device screen
The font-size of the immediate parent element
The height of the body tag
questions.explanation: 'rem' stands for Root EM and is relative to the font-size of the root <html> element (usually 16px by default).

questions.question: Why is 'rem' preferred over 'px' for font sizing in accessible design?
options: rem files are smaller in size
rem respects user browser zoom and font-size accessibility preferences
Browsers refuse to render px fonts on smartphones
questions.explanation: rem units scale automatically when users adjust their system or browser font size settings, unlike fixed px units.

questions.question: What mobile issue does the dynamic viewport unit 'dvh' solve?
options: Dynamic browser URL bars hiding the bottom of 100vh elements on mobile phones
questions.explanation: dvh (dynamic viewport height) recalculates dynamically as browser address bars expand or contract on mobile devices.

questions.question: If an element has font-size: 20px, what does padding: 1.5em evaluate to?
questions.explanation: The 'em' unit is relative to the element's current font-size (1.5 * 20px = 30px).

questions.question: What is 50vw equivalent to in CSS layout?
options: Half of the screen DPI resolution
questions.explanation: 1vw equals 1% of the viewport width, so 50vw is exactly half of the browser viewport width.
